To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The liver biopsies of Parkinsonian patients treated with levodopa plus decarboxylate inhibitor did not show morphological and biochemical changes that could be related to this treatment.”
“Levodopa and Ro 4602 treatment seems not to be toxic for the liver in human patients with Parkinson disease.”
The effects of combined levodopa and Ro4–4602 on liver of parkinsonian patients was studied with morphological and biochemical techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of combined treatment of parkinsonian patients with levodopa (800–100mg) and a decarbo‐xylase inhibitor, 2‐(3,4‐dihydroxyphenyl)‐ethylamine‐N2‐propargyl‐1‐carboxamide (Ro 4–4601), 200–250mg daily.
a study of the liver in Parkinsonian patients treated with levodopa (800–100000 mg) and a decarbo‐xylase inhibitor, (Ro 4–4600 (200–250 mg) daily.
the morphological and biochemical changes occurring in liver biopsies of parkinsonian patients during long‐term treatment with levodop and a decarboxyase inhibitor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver biopsies of parkinsonian patients on levodopa and Ro‐4‐4602 treatment did not reveal any morphological or biochemical evidence of cell injury, and thus no evidence of liver damage.
there is no reason to believe that levodopa and Ro‐4–4602, at the doses used, cause liver cell injury.
the combined treatment with levodop and Ro 4‐4602 is not harmful to the liver of parkinsonian patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
levodopa and Ro‐4–4602 are safe drugs for the treatment of parkinsonian patients.
the liver of patients treated with levodopa plus a decarboxlase inhibitor, does not reveal any morphological or biochemical changes which could be related with the treatment.
the liver is not a target organ for the combined levodopa and Ro‐4–4602 therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of levodopa and carbidopa is a safe and effective treatment option for Parkinson’s disease.
the liver of patients receiving combined treatment with levodop and a decarboylase inhibitor, is not damaged by the treatment.
the use of levodopa with a decarboxylation inhibitor is safe and well tolerated.
